name: Stirling PDF
summary: Merge, split, sign and redact PDFs without uploading them to a stranger's website.

catalog.description: Stirling PDF gives you a private toolbox for everyday document work: merge, split, compress, convert, OCR, sign, redact, and automate PDFs without uploading them to random websites.

screenshots.alt: The Stirling PDF workspace, with the tool list down the left and a household bill open in the document viewer
screenshots.caption: The whole toolbox, with your document already open

screenshots.alt: The Stirling PDF merge tool with six household documents queued as numbered cards, ready to combine into one file
screenshots.caption: Six separate statements into one file, in the order you pick

screenshots.alt: The Stirling PDF redaction tool set to black out a name, beside the payslip it will be applied to
screenshots.caption: Black out a name or a number before you pass it on

screenshots.alt: The Stirling PDF OCR tool set to English, beside a scanned energy bill waiting to be recognised
screenshots.caption: Turn a scan into text you can search, without uploading it anywhere

features.title: Fix everyday PDF problems
features.body: Merge, split, compress, rotate, redact, sign, and convert documents from one private web app.

features.title: Keep sensitive files local
features.body: Run document tools on your own server instead of sending private files to third-party upload sites.

features.title: Automate repeat work
features.body: Use pipelines for repeatable document workflows when the same manual steps keep coming back.

resourceHint.label: Medium resources
resourceHint.description: One service that sits quietly between jobs, but wants a spare gigabyte and a couple of cores while it reads a scan or converts an office document.

privacy.summary: MOS configures the self-hosted server to process ordinary PDF tasks locally and disable known optional analytics.
notes: Persistent app data is kept in package-owned volumes.
User-invoked features such as trusted timestamping can contact an external service.
The assessment is configuration- and documentation-based; it does not prove complete network silence.
